answer_q: How can law firms use AI?
answer: Law firms use AI to screen and route new enquiries, prepare intake and conflict-check information, summarise and search documents, extract key clauses, draft routine correspondence and answer questions from internal precedents. Lawyers remain responsible for advice and review all AI-assisted work.
body:
Why firms are adopting AI carefully

Lawyers spend a large share of their day on work clients don’t value: sorting enquiries, chasing documents, summarising files and answering “where is my matter up to?” At the same time, firms carry strict duties of confidentiality and competence, so careless use of public AI tools is a real risk.

The answer is AI built for the firm, inside controlled systems, with lawyers reviewing anything that becomes advice.

Where AI helps law firms most

Enquiry screening and intake

New enquiries are categorised by practice area, urgency and fit, with key details captured for conflict checks and a booking offered for suitable matters. See custom AI agents.

Document review support

AI summarises long documents, extracts dates, parties and key clauses, and flags issues for lawyer review. See document & data processing.

Precedent and knowledge search

A private assistant answers questions from your precedents, templates and internal guides, with sources cited. See LLM, RAG & knowledge-base bots.

Client updates

Routine matter updates and document requests are drafted and sent on schedule, reducing inbound status calls. See AI workflow automation.

After-hours enquiries

Calls and chat enquiries are answered, captured and booked, without giving legal advice. See AI receptionist.

Human-backed AI employees for law firms

Most law firms don’t want another tool to supervise. Our AI Employees service builds the AI around your firm, then runs it with a dedicated Crenosoft team that learns your services, clients and rules. The AI handles routine work; our reviewers handle anything unusual, around the clock; and decisions that belong to you come to your nominated person with a clear summary. We agree an hours-saved target up front and report against it every month.

Software we connect to

We integrate with practice management and document systems such as LEAP, Actionstep, Smokeball and others with APIs, along with Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Google Workspace, e-signature tools and accounting software.

Confidentiality, privilege and professional duties

Client information never goes into public AI tools. Systems run in controlled environments with access limited by matter and role, and providers are configured so data isn’t used for model training where that option exists. AI assistants don’t give legal advice to the public, and every output that informs advice is reviewed by a lawyer. Victorian practitioners can find guidance on their obligations from the Victorian Legal Services Board + Commissioner.

Across every project we follow the Privacy Act 1988, the OAIC’s guidance on commercially available AI products and our own Responsible AI Policy.

Where to start in a law firm

The safest first projects are those where AI supports lawyers rather than producing advice. Intake screening, document summaries for internal use, precedent search and client status updates all fit this pattern: they save real time, and a lawyer stays in control of anything that matters. Once the firm is comfortable, we look at higher-value work such as first-draft correspondence and due diligence support, always with lawyer review and clear records of how AI was used on each matter.

Results we measure for firms

Before we build, we record a baseline of how long the work takes and how often it happens. After launch, your monthly report tracks the numbers that matter to firms:

  • Enquiries screened and the share converted to consultations
  • Time from enquiry to first response
  • Documents summarised and lawyer hours saved
  • Client status calls avoided through automatic updates
  • Accuracy from lawyer review samples

These figures sit alongside hours saved and accuracy, so you can see exactly what the AI is contributing and where our team is still stepping in.

Every AI-assisted step is logged against the matter, so the firm keeps a clear record of how work was prepared and who reviewed it.

Partners can also see, at a glance, which matters are waiting on clients and which are waiting on the firm.

How to get started

  1. Free AI audit: 30 minutes to map your busiest workflows and pick the first opportunity.
  2. Blueprint and fixed quote: what the AI will do, which systems it connects to and the price in AUD.
  3. Build and test: usually two to six weeks, tested on real examples from your firm.
  4. Launch and improve: monthly reports on hours saved, accuracy and improvements.

Not sure where to begin? Start with an AI Readiness Assessment, or see how we work locally on our Melbourne AI agency page.
faqs: Is it safe for law firms to use AI?

It can be, with the right controls: private systems rather than public chatbots, access limited by matter, providers configured to keep data out of training, and lawyer review of anything that informs advice.
AI can summarise contracts, extract key clauses and flag unusual terms to speed up review. A lawyer still reviews the document and gives the advice.
Will an AI intake assistant give legal advice?
No. It captures details, categorises the enquiry and books a consultation where appropriate. Legal advice only comes from your lawyers.
Yes. A knowledge-base assistant can answer questions from your precedents and templates, with links to the source documents, respecting access permissions.
